Brighton and Hove is a thriving area with strong demand for reliable boiler repair and servicing services. Local properties range from period Victorian and Edwardian homes through to modern new-build developments, each presenting different plumbing requirements and challenges.

Our Gas Safe registered engineers serve all areas of Brighton and Hove and the surrounding East Sussex region. Whether you're in the town centre or the surrounding residential areas, we provide prompt, professional boiler repair services with transparent pricing and no hidden call-out charges.

With years of experience working across East Sussex, our engineers understand the specific plumbing challenges faced by local homeowners. From the older pipe infrastructure common in period properties to the modern systems found in newer developments, our team has the expertise to handle any boiler repair and servicing requirement.

We cover all postcodes across Brighton and Hove with same-day availability for urgent work. All our engineers are fully qualified, insured, and committed to leaving your property clean and tidy after every job.

faqs.q: My boiler is making a banging noise — what does it mean?
faqs.a: Banging, kettling, or clunking sounds usually indicate limescale buildup on the heat exchanger, a failing pump, or trapped air in the system. All are repairable by a qualified engineer.

faqs.q: How long does a boiler repair take?
faqs.a: Most boiler repairs take 1-3 hours. If specialist parts need ordering, the initial visit diagnoses the fault and the repair is completed on a second visit typically within 24-48 hours.

faqs.q: Can I use my boiler while it is making an error code?
faqs.a: Depends on the code. Some error codes allow limited operation; others indicate a dangerous fault that requires immediate shutdown. Never ignore a gas smell — turn off at the gas meter and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

faqs.q: Is boiler repair covered by home insurance?
faqs.a: Standard home insurance rarely covers boiler repair. Boiler cover policies (British Gas, Homeserve, etc.) typically cover parts and labour for an annual fee. Check your existing policy before purchasing additional cover.

localParagraph: Brighton and Hove presents a genuinely varied challenge for boiler engineers, given the mix of Victorian terraces in Kemp Town and Hove's Poets' Corner, mid-century purpose-built flats along the seafront, and newer developments further inland toward Portslade. Each property era brings its own heating system quirks — older homes often have ageing conventional boilers tied to gravity-fed systems, while more recent builds tend to feature combi units that require a different diagnostic approach. Water hardness across Brighton and Hove sits in a mixed range, meaning limescale accumulation inside heat exchangers and around valves is a real consideration for residents in certain postcodes, though not uniformly severe. Engineers working locally will typically check for scale build-up and advise on inhibitor treatments accordingly. As part of England's coastal south-east, the region also sees damp conditions that can accelerate corrosion on external flue terminals and condensate pipework. Prompt repair work, carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers familiar with the area's housing stock, helps extend boiler lifespan and keeps energy bills from creeping upward unnecessarily.
whatItInvolves: Boiler repair covers fault diagnosis and component replacement to restore a failing or broken boiler to full working order. Common faults include pressure loss, ignition failure, pump failure, heat exchanger leaks, PCB failure, and faulty diverter valves. A qualified Gas Safe engineer will identify the root cause — not just reset the fault code.
process: The engineer connects a diagnostic reader to your boiler's PCB to extract fault codes, then conducts a systematic inspection of the key components: heat exchanger, pump, igniter, gas valve, pressure relief valve, and expansion vessel. Once the fault is identified you'll receive a fixed repair quote. Parts are ordered and fitted on the same visit where possible, or next-day for specialist components.
whatToExpect: Most boiler repairs are completed in 1-3 hours. Always ask for a written report of the fault and the work carried out — you'll need this if the boiler fails again under guarantee. If the repair cost exceeds 50% of a new boiler's value, a replacement is usually better value long-term.
